html:
SMTO-CMP-0001 — Answer preserved

GUID: 7598dbb5-2043-47b6-b0b8-54983d7e83dc
Slug: final-response-structure
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The Agent finished with an answer but didn't mark the task as done in the way SMTO requires. Your answer and any work already done are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the Agent's answer in the conversation and check its results, such as files or messages it says it made. SMTO kept the answer but couldn't confirm the task ended the required way.
  2. If something is missing, reply asking the Agent to finish that part and say when it's done. A follow-up lets the Agent finish properly instead of repeating the same ending.
  3. If the work is complete and the task shows a card named Require explicit completion, you can turn off Enforce this check for this run. SMTO then checks the saved answer again for this run only, without redoing any work.

What success looks like

  • The task shows as completed, or the Agent's next reply finishes the remaining work.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the whole request again from scratch; that could repeat work that's already done.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The run kept the Agent's final answer, but its completion declaration did not meet the strict completion structure check (completion.strict_final_response_structure); the answer and successful tool results were preserved.

What this means

  • Retained-final-response handling identifies completion structure/protocol defects and, when its configured strict check applies, preserves the candidate while exposing structure feedback. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Retained-final-response handling identifies completion structure/protocol defects and, when its configured strict check applies, preserves the candidate while exposing structure feedback.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retained candidate text, structure_errors and the effective explicit-completion setting separately from receipt validity.

How to fix it

  • Inspect final_response_feedback.reason and the candidate's terminal_parse_errors in the run state. Resolve through the supported paths: let the automatic correction step run, use the per-run override of the Require explicit completion check (which re-evaluates the kept answer without new model or tool calls), or follow up in the conversation; don't regenerate completed work.
  • Use the supported retained-response reevaluation or exact declaration-correction flow; preserve completed work and follow the effective completion policy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported reevaluation or declaration correction uses the retained answer and original receipts.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
